column1: # Retail code written as assembly: original assembly, finished work that no C
# source can or should reproduce. Read by tools/handwritten_asm.py (structure in
# CI, the evidence against the retail bytes with --retail) and counted by
# tools/progress_status.py in a column of its own, never as accepted C; the
# ByteMatch report does not count it.
# The rule is the one OpenRAC/rac1-decomp states in docs/game/asm-classification.md
# and rac2-decomp and rac3-decomp apply with ASM_FUNC: a function is original
# assembly when it holds an instruction the pinned C chains never emit. Inline
# assembly is not C evidence here (docs/gates/boot-match-scope.md), so such a
# body has no C form. `sync` and `sync.p` alone are not evidence, because the
# pinned sdk991111sync chain emits them from __builtin_rac5_sync. A row is one
# whole report unit (a boot interval up to the next label, or a level shape
# unit) that is one routine carrying the evidence, or only syscall trampolines;
# a unit whose evidence lies in one of several functions stays open
# scope    boot, or the level module of the shape unit's first placement
# name     boot: the report unit label; levels: the shape unit name
# start    boot: virtual address; levels: offset in the module
# bytes    the unit's code bytes, as progress/report.json counts them
#          mmi       128-bit MMI operations ee-gcc has no pattern for (the moves
#          syscall   nothing but syscall trampolines (addiu $v1 / syscall / jr $ra / nop)
# evidence what the retail bytes hold, and the sister project that keeps an
#          identical twin as handwritten assembly, when one does
